items.headline: Houthi missile barrage on Saudi Arabia and Iranian threat to widen war send Brent above $106
items.summary: Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea cities of Yanbu (a key oil export terminal) and Taif; Saudi air defenses intercepted six. A senior Iranian military official separately warned Tehran could broaden the roughly seven-month-old Iran war into the Indian Ocean if attacked, sending Brent up ~3.3% to ~$106.45 and WTI up ~2.4% to ~$94.39.
items.actionable: Escalation risk supports a safe-haven bid for gold/silver but the accompanying yield spike and risk-off tone are pressuring miners and broad equities simultaneously, so the net read for the book is ambiguous rather than a clean tailwind.

items.headline: US and Iran explore phased deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz, ease blockade
items.summary: Negotiators meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, mediated by Qatar, Pakistan and Egypt, are discussing a roadmap for a regionwide ceasefire of up to 60 days, phased reopening of Hormuz and an end to the US naval blockade of Iran. Trump has ruled out lifting the blockade before Iran shows sufficient goodwill, and oil pulled back from session highs on the report.
items.actionable: A credible de-escalation path caps further oil-driven safe-haven demand for metals and could reverse some of Thursday's flight-to-safety flow into gold/silver if talks progress over the weekend.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield hits highest since 2007 as Fed's hawkish pivot compounds oil shock
items.summary: Surging Treasury yields (~5.0-5.1%, a level last seen in 2007) combined with the oil-driven geopolitical shock pushed the S&P 500 down slightly and the Nasdaq lower on Thursday. The move follows the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% under new Chair Kevin Warsh on 16 Sep, with nine of eighteen officials projecting a further 2026 hike.
items.actionable: Rising long-end yields at a 19-year high compress valuations across the REIT/developer book (Keppel REIT, Mapletree trusts, CDL, UOL) and add to funding-cost pressure, arguing against deploying the cash pile aggressively into rate-sensitive names right now.

items.headline: Gold and silver slide as dollar rallies on firming Fed hike bets
items.summary: Spot gold fell toward $4,273-4,308/oz (down ~1.1%) and spot silver dropped to $64-65/oz (down ~2.9%) as the US dollar hit a two-month high on growing conviction the Fed will hike again in October and possibly December. This is the pullback that carried into Thursday's close, where miners eased slightly despite the oil/geopolitical spike.
items.actionable: The dollar-driven pullback in gold/silver is the direct near-term risk to the levered silver and miner sleeve of the book; watch whether the metals decouple positively if Hormuz talks fail and the Iran war escalates further, which would offset the rate-driven headwind.

items.headline: Fed hikes rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% under new Chair Warsh, first hike since 2023, signals more to come
items.summary: The FOMC voted to raise the fed funds rate 25bp, reversing prior cut expectations, as persistent inflation and energy-shock pressures forced a hawkish pivot under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Updated dot-plot projections show 9 of 18 officials expecting at least one more hike this year.
items.actionable: A hawkish, still-hiking Fed is the single biggest headwind for the silver/gold miners leg of the book via a stronger dollar and higher real yields, while it is a structural tailwind for the DBS/OCBC net-interest-margin story and a further drag on SGX REIT valuations.

items.headline: China's rare-earth magnet exports to US plunge 21% ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
items.summary: Chinese customs data show magnet shipments to the US fell to 512 tons in August from the month before, a 21% drop, as Beijing leverages its dominance (JL Mag alone is projected to retain ~80% of global magnet output by 2030) even as Trump and Xi extended their trade truce to mid-January 2027. Bloomberg frames magnets as China's single greatest point of leverage in trade negotiations.
items.actionable: A deliberate squeeze on magnet exports even alongside a truce extension directly strengthens the investment case for the Western rare-earth watchlist (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth, Neo, Iluka) as buyers scramble for non-China supply.

items.headline: Iluka signs binding rare-earths offtake with global automaker for Eneabba output
items.summary: Iluka Resources locked in a four-year binding offtake (starting 2028, ~1,200 tonnes of NdPr/Dy/Tb oxides, take-or-pay pricing) with an unnamed global automotive company. The Eneabba refinery, backed by A$1.65bn in non-recourse Australian government financing, is over 50% built and targeting mid-2027 commissioning.
items.actionable: A binding automotive offtake with government-backed financing de-risks Iluka's non-China magnet-material supply chain and reinforces the broader thesis that Western/allied rare-earth names on the watchlist are converting policy support into commercial contracts.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls to ~$83-84k as hawkish Fed rate-hike bets weigh on crypto
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped roughly 2% to trade near $83,462 and Ethereum fell to about $2,646 on Thursday as markets priced a 75.3% chance of an October Fed hike and 58.6% for December. Separately, NYSE and Blockchain.com signed an MOU to explore tokenized US stocks/ETFs for Blockchain.com's 44 million+ verified users.
items.actionable: Crypto selling off in sympathy with the same hawkish-Fed/strong-dollar dynamic hitting silver confirms this is a broad risk-asset repricing rather than metals-specific, relevant context if considering where to deploy the cash pile once rate expectations stabilize.

items.headline: Jefferies initiates Singapore banks: Buy DBS and UOB, Hold OCBC
items.summary: Jefferies started coverage citing the banks' proven resilience across credit cycles, superior capital generation, and further scope for earnings/dividend compounding, with OCBC initiated at Hold (the lowest rating of the three). The call comes as rising SORA following the Fed hike is seen restoring net interest margins after years of compression.
items.actionable: Fresh sell-side conviction on DBS/UOB reinforces the case that the Singapore bank leg of the book is the direct beneficiary of the same hawkish Fed pivot that is hurting the silver/gold miners leg -- a natural internal hedge within the portfolio.

items.headline: S-REITs down 8.2% YTD even as STI up 24.6%, gap widened by higher-for-longer rates
items.summary: The iEdge S-REIT Index has fallen 8.2% year-to-date while the broader Straits Times Index has surged 24.6%, a divergence driven almost entirely by DBS, OCBC and UOB. Rising rates compress REIT valuations through higher refinancing costs, less competitive yields versus risk-free rates, and higher cap rates pressuring asset values.
items.actionable: The bank/REIT performance gap is set to persist or widen given the confirmed Fed hiking cycle, keeping Keppel REIT, Mapletree trusts and CapitaLand REIT exposure under structural pressure relative to the DBS/OCBC/UOB holdings in the same book.

items.headline: Xiaomi flags margin pressure from component costs; EV unit passes 500,000 cumulative deliveries
items.summary: Xiaomi management warned of continued pressure from elevated component costs, slow demand recovery and intense competition in its core devices business. Separately, its EV arm passed 500,000 cumulative SU7 deliveries and outlined plans (unveiled at IFA 2026) to launch electric cars in Europe by 2027.
items.actionable: The EV delivery milestone and Europe expansion plan are longer-term positives for the growth narrative, but the explicit near-term margin warning on component costs is a reason to expect continued earnings volatility in the Xiaomi position.

items.headline: Hang Seng roughly flat as mainland China stocks fall, Tencent dips
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index shed just a fraction of a percent as regional risk-off sentiment tied to the Mideast escalation and surging Treasury yields weighed on mainland equities more than Hong Kong. Tencent closed lower, down about 0.6-1.0%, while semiconductor and AI-hardware names showed relative resilience.
items.actionable: HK tech held up better than mainland China against Thursday's global risk-off move, suggesting the Tencent position is currently more exposed to broad macro/yield sentiment than to any fresh company- or regulatory-specific catalyst.

items.headline: US export-control regime keeps SMIC capped at low-tens-of-thousands 7nm wafers/month
items.summary: A presumption-of-denial licensing standard remains in force for most items destined to SMIC, and Commerce has extended validity dates on high-bandwidth-memory-related controls to December 2026. Analysts estimate China's advanced-chip output remains at only 1-4% of US production capacity, constraining SMIC's ability to scale 5nm/7nm production.
items.actionable: The tightening/extension of US chip controls is a persistent structural ceiling on SMIC's leading-edge ambitions, reinforcing that the SMIC position is a longer-horizon China-self-sufficiency bet rather than a near-term re-rating catalyst.

note: Active alternate 2026 macro backdrop: the Fed HIKED (not cut) 25bp on 16 Sep to 3.75-4.00% under new Chair Kevin Warsh amid an ongoing ~7-month US-Iran war, and the 10-year Treasury yield is at its highest since 2007 -- this hawkish, high-yield regime is the dominant driver behind Thursday's oil spike, gold/silver pullback, crypto weakness, SG bank strength and REIT underperformance. 5 items above are dated 23-24 Sep (last 24-48h), satisfying the freshness requirement. Two candidate items (a Nov-2025-dated CapitaLand-Mapletree merger story, and stale Jan/Mar-2026 rare-earth funding items) were excluded as out-of-window rather than padded in.
